title: ProperPicTorsionBaseChange
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension], and let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a smooth separated connected proper curve [def-sc-curves]. Let $n\geq1$ be nonzero in $k$. For the Picard groups of invertible modules [def-sc-picard-group], there is a bijection $F:\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]\to\operatorname{Pic}(C_K)[n]$ with $F(L)=\pi^*L$ for every line bundle class, where $\pi:C_K\to C$ is the projection.

source.place: proper-case degree-one paragraph: Jacobian n-torsion comparison

proof.text: Apply baseChange_curve to get a connected smooth proper curve after extension. For each curve, exists_mulEquiv_prod_picZero provides the degree-zero subgroup and a multiplicative degree coordinate. If L^n=1, applying that coordinate gives n deg(L)=0 in Z; since n is nonzero, deg(L)=0. Thus every torsion class belongs to the respective degree-zero subgroup.

Construct p as Pic.mapHom of the pullback projection. Hom.picDegree_eq identifies degree with the degree of the representative module, fromSkeletonToSkeletonIso identifies the representative of its Picard pullback with the actual module pullback, and Modules.degree_pullback preserves degree. Consequently p restricts to a multiplicative homomorphism j between the two degree-zero subgroups, with underlying value exactly p.
Apply picZero_torsion_base_change to j and the nonvanishing of n in k. It gives injectivity of j and a torsion lift of every degree-zero torsion class after extension.

Define F on torsion classes by F(L)=(p(L), map_pow p L n and L^n=1). For injectivity, regard both source torsion classes as elements of G, use equality of their images to invoke injectivity of j, and take subgroup values. For surjectivity, regard a target torsion class as an element y of Gprime, lift it to x in G with x^n=1 and j(x)=y, and take the class x.val. Subtype.ext proves both equalities; the required value equation for F is definitional.
